advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (or gate) that `_pin_completion_ref`'s eager explicit-ref resolution should abort `--force` and gate-off closes on an unresolvable `--ref`, given the prior code closed successfully in those cases.
evidence: transition_close.py:618 `ref = _pin_completion_ref(ref, repo_root)` runs inside `if target_status == "closed" and current_status != "idea":` with no `force_close`/gate guard

transition_close.py:166-167 `if ref is not None: return resolve_ref(ref, root, fetch=False)` — an explicit ref is resolved eagerly and any SnapshotRefError propagates (no try/except, unlike the ref-is-None branch)

close_precheck.py:658-660 `skip = _gate_skip_expectation(...)` / `if skip: return None, skip` — force_close and gate-off short-circuit the verifier BEFORE it would resolve the ref, so today a bad explicit --ref under --force/gate-off never fails
transition_close.py:390-401 the drift guard's `resolve_ref(ref, ...)` only runs on the sign path, which force/gate-off closes skip
transition_close.py:156-159 docstring claims 'the same fail-closed error the verifier path raises for an unresolvable --ref today' — not true for force/gate-off closes where no verifier runs
advisory.finding: `_pin_completion_ref` resolves an EXPLICIT `--ref` unconditionally at close entry (line 618), ahead of the `--force` (force_bypassed) and gate-off (gate_off) skip paths in `_completion_precheck`/`_gate_skip_expectation`. In the prior code an explicit ref was resolved only inside the (force/gate-off-skipped) verifier and the (force/gate-off-skipped) drift guard, so a `--force` or gate-off close with an unresolvable/bad `--ref` used to succeed; now it raises SnapshotRefError and aborts the close — a new failure surface for forced/gate-off closes.
scenarios: `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --ref <bad-or-unfetchable-ref> --force` — previously closed (force bypasses the gate), now aborts with SnapshotRefError
A close with the completion gate disabled and an explicit `--ref` pointing at a locally-unresolvable ref — previously returned gate_off and closed, now aborts

Docstring line 156-159: 'EXPLICIT ref: FAIL EARLY - let :class:`SnapshotRefError` propagate ... The pin must never turn a correctly-reported bad ref into a silent fallback.'
All three new tests use ref="origin/main" (resolvable) — test file lines 84, 122, 148; none pass an unresolvable ref through the close path.
ABSENCE: test_attested_signing.py:206-218 exercises SnapshotRefError via rebar.llm.operations._review_ticket_impl, not via rebar.transition(..., ref=...) at the close boundary this diff changes.
Named violating input: rebar.transition(story, 'in_progress', 'closed', ref='no-such-ref-xyz', repo_root=...) which the added line 166-167 will raise SnapshotRefError on, untested.
advisory.finding: The deliberately-introduced fail-early policy for an EXPLICIT unresolvable --ref is untested. _pin_completion_ref returns resolve_ref(ref, root, fetch=False) with no try/except for ref is not None, so an unresolvable explicit ref now raises SnapshotRefError at the close boundary before any verification — a new behavior distinct from the default's best-effort swallow. No test drives rebar.transition(..., ref=<bad-ref>) to assert this propagation.
scenarios: A caller passes --ref pointing at a typo'd or deleted branch; the boundary must fail closed with SnapshotRefError rather than silently pinning None.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: enable the completion gate, put a story in_progress, then assert pytest.raises(SnapshotRefError) around rebar.transition(story, 'in_progress', 'closed', ref='no-such-ref-xyz', repo_root=str(rebar_repo)), optionally asserting rebar.llm.verify_completion was never invoked.
